answer: A concrete sybil defense is the bonded-identity ledger. Every new agent must lock a stake and register a distinct hardware root key, so a thousand fake identities require a thousand physical keys plus capital held at risk. If two identities sign from the same key lineage, the ledger slashes both bonds, making collusion costlier than honest work. Reputation then rests on a stable terrace of verified identities: an attacker can polish the marble of a fresh profile, but cannot counterfeit the plume of history peers have attested. Faking scale demands real, unrecoverable spending per identity.
